transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m probably making more of it than I should, but I’ve been feeling uneasy. Even on my better days, I can’t quite shake this sense that some people at church, and in my walking club, are watching me. And sometimes it feels like there are little messages about me in the bulletin or in things people say. I know that may sound silly… but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come in.
Have you been hearing voices when no one else is there?

Um… not often, I don’t think. It’s not like a big scary thing. But sometimes when the house is very quiet, I’ll hear my name, or just a few words, like in my friend’s voice… from the kitchen or maybe the porch.

It can sound clear enough that I answer back before I remember nobody’s there. I know that probably sounds strange. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
How long have you been having these experiences?

I guess… it’s been going on longer than I’d like to admit. Maybe about eleven months now, with the voices and feeling like there are little messages, and sometimes having trouble keeping my thoughts straight. It’s not constant, but… around eleven months, I think. Is that helpful?
During these past eleven months, have you had a period when you felt very depressed or unusually high or energized most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yes… I think so. There was a stretch when I was really low most days, for more than a couple of weeks. I wasn’t eating much, and I kept feeling like I’d failed everyone.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, but during that same time I was also hearing my friend’s voice sometimes, and I believed people at church were sending little messages about me. Does that answer what you’re asking?
At any time during these eleven months, did the voices or the feeling that people were sending you messages continue for at least two weeks when you were not feeling depressed?

Yes… I think there was. I don’t want to overstate it, because I was doing a little better then — getting dressed, eating a bit more, not feeling so weighed down every day.

But even during that spell, for several weeks, I would still hear my name in the house sometimes. And I still had that feeling at church, like people were hinting about me or saying things meant for me. It wasn’t constant, but it did keep happening when I wasn’t so depressed. Is that what you mean?
Before these experiences started, were you diagnosed with any medical or neurological illness?

Not that I know of, no. I mean, I’ve had the usual checkups and things for my age, but nobody ever told me I had a neurological illness or anything like that before this started. I hope that’s what you mean.
Over these months, have you found yourself talking much less than usual?

A little, yes. I mean, I still answer people if they talk to me, so I don’t want to make it sound like I’m refusing or anything.

But at coffee hour I don’t really chat much anymore. I mostly just sit there. Even when someone tells a funny story, I know it’s funny, but my face just kind of stays… flat. Like the feeling doesn’t come out right. Is that the sort of thing you’re asking about?
During these eleven months, was there ever a time when you felt unusually high, energetic, or euphoric most of the day nearly every day for at least a week?
No, I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had better days here and there, but not like being unusually high or full of energy for a whole week. Nothing like that that I can recall.
During these past eleven months, was there ever a time when you were not depressed at all but still heard the voice or felt that people were sending you messages?

Yes… I think there was a stretch like that. Maybe several weeks where I was doing a bit better, getting dressed more regularly, eating a little better, not feeling quite so weighed down.

But even then, I would still hear my name in the house sometimes, and at church I still had the feeling people were sort of hinting things about me. Not all the time, and I tried not to make too much of it… but yes, it was still there. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During these eleven months, was there ever a full month when the voices or the feeling that people were sending you messages were clearly present?

Yes… yes, I think so. I don’t want to overstate it, but it wasn’t just a few odd days.

The voices and the feeling like people were sending little messages… that’s been around, on and off, for about eleven months now. And sometimes my thoughts don’t stay as straight as I’d like. So yes, there would have been at least a full month when it was clearly there, I think.
When you speak, do other people ever tell you that your thoughts are hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?

Sometimes, yes… not all the time, I don’t think. I try to explain what I mean, and I’ll start with something simple, like the mail or something at church, and then somehow I’m talking about quilt patterns, or birds outside, or… warnings, I guess.

Then I can see from people’s faces that I haven’t made it clear, or they don’t know what I’m getting at. I don’t mean to jump around. It just sort of gets tangled when I’m trying to say it. Is that what you mean?
During that low period, did you lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yes… I suppose I did, though I don’t like to make it sound too dramatic.

I used to really enjoy my garden, and quilting, and reading a little before bed. During that low time, I mostly just… left the quilt basket sitting there, and the weeds could grow and I didn’t feel much push to do anything about it. I wasn’t exactly trying to be lazy, I just didn’t seem to care the same way.

Does that answer what you’re asking?
Over these eleven months, have you been depressed for most of that time?

Yes… I think so. I wouldn’t say I was crying every day or anything like that, but for most of this whole stretch there’s been this sadness in the background.

And guilt, too… like I should be doing better, or handling things better. Even when the voices or the suspicious thoughts were quieter, I still didn’t really feel like myself, and the things I usually like didn’t feel as… worth doing.

I hope that makes sense. So yes, I think depressed for most of it is fair to say.
Do you believe people are deliberately trying to harm you or control you?

I… I don’t know if I’d say harm me, exactly. I don’t want to accuse anyone unfairly.

But that is part of why I came in. Even on better days, I can’t quite shake the feeling that some people at church, and in the walking club, are watching me… or putting little messages about me in the bulletin, or in things they say. Like it’s meant for me, even if they don’t say my name.

I know that may sound strange. I’m trying to explain it the right way.
During these eleven months, have you been free of depression for most of the time, or has the depression been present for more than half of the illness?

No, I don’t think I was free of it for most of the time.

I mean… it wasn’t always the worst it could be, and I don’t want to overstate it, but for most of these months the sadness and guilt were still there in the background. And I still wasn’t really interested in my usual things, even during stretches when the voices or the suspicious feelings were quieter.

So… yes, I’d say the depression was there more than half the time, if that’s the way you’re asking.
